source.title: Instant transformation of learned repulsion into motivational "wanting".

confidence_rationale: Behavioural + Fos demonstration that incentive salience attaches to a SPECIFIC, discrete object-cue (a particular inserted lever) and is REVALUABLE on the fly -- a previously-repulsive object becomes an avidly-approached motivational magnet at first re-encounter in a new state. This grounds two of SD-057's pillars: object-specific binding of incentive value, and the revaluability of the per-object token (MECH-345). Discounted because the revaluation here is driven by physiological state, so it partly overlaps MECH-436's territory rather than isolating the object-binding architecture cleanly.
failure_signatures: The object-specific incentive transformation was driven by a physiological state change (sodium depletion); the paper does not isolate object-binding from drive-state modulation, so it cannot by itself distinguish SD-057's per-object token from MECH-436's drive gain acting on a single value.
Behaviour was directed at one discrete lever-cue; the competitive selection of a most-wanted object AMONG several simultaneously-represented object tokens (SD-057's argmax-seed step) is not tested.

mapping.source_claim_statement: A discrete Pavlovian cue (a briefly-inserted metal lever) that had always predicted an unpleasant intense-salt taste, and toward which rats had learned active repulsion, was instantly transformed into an attractive motivational magnet -- approached, jumped on, and gnawed -- the first time it was re-encountered in a novel sodium-depletion state, with elevated Fos in VTA, nucleus accumbens, ventral pallidum and orbitofrontal cortex; desire is recomputed at re-encounter by integrating Pavlovian information with current physiological state, not read off a cached learned value.
mapping.ree_translation: SD-057's per-object incentive layer (MECH-345) posits a per-object slow-decay REVALUABLE incentive token whose wanting amplitude is recomputed at recall. Robinson & Berridge show incentive value is bound to a SPECIFIC discrete object and can be revalued -- even sign-reversed -- without re-learning, which is exactly the revaluable, object-bound token SD-057 maintains rather than a single overwritten attractor conflating liking and wanting.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The revaluation is driven by physiological (salt-depletion) state, so the demonstration entangles object-binding (SD-057) with drive-state modulation (MECH-436); it supports that incentive value is object-specific and revaluable but does not separate those two mechanisms. Also a single-object behavioural test -- the cross-object competition that SD-057's most-wanted argmax requires is untested.
mapping.source_context: Rat behaviour (autoshaping/approach to an inserted lever-CS predicting Dead-Sea-salt taste) plus Fos immunohistochemistry of mesocorticolimbic activation; induced sodium-depletion vs normal state.

confidence_components.notes: Solid behavioural + Fos study. Mapping discounted because object-binding and drive-state revaluation are entangled here, and cross-object competition is not tested.
